questions.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 8\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -8 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}4 \\ -2 \\ 8\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ -8 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}4{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-2 \\ -2{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-8 \\ 8{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & -2 \\ -2 & 2 & -8 \\ 8 & 2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & ↔{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -8 \\ 4 & 2 & -2 \\ 8 & 2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & 6 & -18 \\ 8 & 2 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & 6 & -18 \\ 0 & 10 & k-32\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{6}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 10 & k-32\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-10{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-2 & 2 & -8 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & k-2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-2.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-2\,⟹\,k=2.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 6\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 5 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=2 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=5 \\ 3{x}_{1}+6{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 2 & -1 & 5 \\ 3 & 6 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & 6 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 9 & k-6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-9{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & k-15\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-15.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-15\,⇒\,k=15.
$$

questions.problem:
Find the values of $k$ such that the vector $b$ lies in $\text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\},$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,b=[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5 \\ k\end{aligned}].
$$
questions.worked_solution:
We know that $b\in \text{Span}\{{a}_{1},{a}_{2}\}$ if there exist ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2} & =b \\ {x}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+{x}_{2}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 2 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}9 \\ -5 \\ k\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=9 \\ 3{x}_{1}+2{x}_{2}=-5 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}=k\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 3 & 2 & -5 \\ 2 & -1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 8 & -32 \\ 2 & -1 & k\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 8 & -32 \\ 0 & 3 & k-18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{8}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 3 & k-18\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}-3{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 9 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & k-6\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The third row of the augmented matrix now corresponds to the equation $0{x}_{1}+0{x}_{2}=k-6.$ Therefore, the system has a solution only if

$$
0=k-6\,⇒\,k=6.
$$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,3,2⟩$, $c=⟨2,-1,-1⟩$, and  $u=⟨5,-5,-4⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -5 \\ -4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-s+2t=5 \\ 3s-t=-5 \\ 2s-t=-4\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 3 & -1 & -5 \\ 2 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 2 & -1 & -4\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 5 & 10 \\ 0 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 3 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-3){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-s+2t=5 \\ t=2 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=2.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s+2t & =5 \\ -s+2(2) & =5 \\ -s+4 & =5 \\ s & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-1,\,t=2,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-b+2c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-1)\cdot 2=-2.$

questions.problem: Determine if the vector $u$ lies on the plane $Π:r=sb+tc,$ $t,s\in R$, where  $b=⟨-1,-1,4⟩$, $c=⟨-3,-8,14⟩$, and  $u=⟨5,-10,-14⟩.$ In the affirmative case, find the value of $s\cdot t$ from the decomposition $u=sb+tc.$
questions.worked_solution:
By definition, $u\in Π$ if there exist $t$ and $s$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}sb+tc & =u \\ s[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+t[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -8 \\ 14\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -10 \\ -14\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the following system of equations:

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-s-3t=5 \\ -s-8t=-10 \\ 4s+14t=-14\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system above, we set up and row reduce an augmented matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ -1 & -8 & -10 \\ 4 & 14 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -15 \\ 4 & 14 & -14\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & -5 & -15 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :=-\frac{1}{5}{R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & 6\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-2){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-1 & -3 & 5 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we have the system

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-s-3t=5 \\ t=3 \\ 0=0.\end{aligned}
$$

From the second equation, we get

$$
t=3.
$$

Substituting into the first equation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-s-3t & =5 \\ -s-3(3) & =5 \\ -s-9 & =5 \\ s & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$

Since we found a solution $s=-14,\,t=3,$ we conclude that $u$ does indeed lie on the plane $Π.$ In fact, we have

$$
u=-14b+3c.
$$

Finally, $s\cdot t=(-14)\cdot 3=-42.$
